item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes addressed the free-agent status of longtime veteran Kiké Hernández. Where the Dodgers stand with Kike Hernandez Hernandez is once again a free agen t after a season with the Dodgers, though this time his return does not seem as imminent as before. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) During the MLB General Managers’ meetings, Gomes was asked about the pending free agent as the days count down until the lockout. “I think Kiké’s been such a huge part of what we’ve done in the past and we’ll continue to have those conversations, but what that looks like right now, I don’t know,” Gomes said of Hernandez. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Enrique Hernandez (8) reacts after losing the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs to the Milwaukee Brewers at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Seemingly, as Hernandez and the Dodgers try to assess his market and weigh possible upgrades, there is still an open line of communication, which opens a path for a reunion down the line. However, factors may lead the team to bring in some fresh blood to the batting order. Why the Dodgers may not bring back Hernandez Last year, the Dodgers and Hernandez did a bit of song and dance before he re-signed ahead of Spring Training. Despite recovering from elbow surgery, he agreed to a one-year, $5 million contract and started the season on the injured list until May, when he came back, just to once again get hurt, this time with an abdominal tear. He missed another handful of months before coming back for the end of the season and the postseason. Over the regular season, he hit .222/.271/.400 in 41 games, with four home runs, 12 RBIs, 28 strikeouts, and just six walks. Oct 14, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Enrique Hernandez (8) reacts to striking out against the Milwaukee Brewers during the sixth inning in game three of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The postseason, aside from a big home run in the NLDS, was no different: 1-for-14 with no walks and three strikeouts. With elbow injuries impacting him over the last two years, along with the abdominal injury, Hernandez’s injury record has become somewhat alarming, and at age 35, is it possible for things to get better? The Dodgers felt like an old squad that could use some new blood, and if they want to pave the way for younger position players, letting Hernandez go could be a reasonable move.

item.title: Steelers center Zach Frazier tabbed as midseason First-Team All-Pro
item.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line has been the most pleasant surprise of the season so far. Pittsburgh has one of the best rushing attacks in the entire league through nine weeks, averaging 117.9 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s offensive line is finally turning the corner and emerging as a serious strength of the team, and it all starts with their center, Zach Frazier. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell put together his midseason All-Pro team , with the Steelers center earning first-team honors. Frazier’s 79.5 overall PFF grade is first among centers this season. The center has posted his best grades as a run and pass blocker of his career this season. New column: My midseason awards + All-Pro team https://t.co/TywmDBPYUr pic.twitter.com/U1ckcuHeFm — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) November 12, 2026 As well as being named to Barnwell’s midseason All-Pro team, Frazier was also named a top contender for the Protector of the Year award. “With Creed Humphrey’s problems snapping the football becoming more conspicuous, Frazier has emerged for me as the best center in football,” Barnwell said. “The Steelers have quietly fielded one of the league’s most efficient run games this season, and so much of that is what Frazier is able to do as the pivot. Watch here, as he reaches and manhandles Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger to spring Jaylen Warren for a 24-yard gain. Frazier has also given up only one sack and four quick pressures all season, per NFL Next Gen Stats.” There is no denying that Frazier is putting together the best season of his career. The 51st overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft is due for an extension this summer that will almost certainly make him one of, if not the highest-paid center in the league. Frazier will continue to be one of the Steelers’ key building blocks for years to come, and he’s finally getting the attention he deserves. Let us know what you think in the comments . item.title: Texas State RB commit Daylon Gordon, a top 2027 Bobcats pledge, flips to Ohio State
item.description: Wylie's Daylon Gordon (1) carries the ball against Wylie East during the second half of a high school football game at Wylie ISD Stadium in Wylie, Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. (Chitose Suzuki/The Dallas Morning News) It's not too often a loss on the recruiting trail can show the strength of a team's scouting prowess, but that might be the case for Texas State football. Daylon Gordon, a running back who pledged to the Bobcats in the spring, has reportedly flipped his commitment to Ohio State. The 5-foot-9 senior out of Wylie was a three-star recruit at the time but has risen up the 247Sports rankings. He's now a four-star prospect overall and according to the site's composite. He was the 33rd-ranked back in the nation but has risen to No. 22. Last season, Gordon rushed 169 times for 1,063 yards and 14 TDs, per 247Sports. He also added 38 receptions for 565 yards and four TDs on a sturdy 14.9 yards per catch. Gabe Brooks, a scouting analyst for 247, wrote in May that Gordon is a "dynamic playmaker" as both a pass catcher and ball carrier. "Natural build for the position with a low center of gravity and broad-shouldered stature," he wrote. "Solid track and field data accompanies equally respectable testing numbers." Brooks also praised his top-end speed and acceleration. So it's no surprise the Buckeyes would be interested. He also held offers from Texas Tech, Utah, Florida State, Ole Miss and others. Texas State head coach GJ Kinne still has one potential back committed in the class: Isaiah Reed, who is listed by some recruiting outlets as an ATH, out of Hamshire. item.description: UTSA Roadrunners running back Will Henderson III (1) celebrates after rushing for a touchdown during the second quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. "Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press on toward the goal," the verse reads. Traylor said real coaching starts in the face of adversity, and the Roadrunners met plenty in a 60-29 loss at FAU last Thursday that ended UTSA's unbeaten run through the American Conference. In his seventh year leading the program, Traylor knows longtime observers and even some of the players have likely grown tired of hearing his familiar mantras, but he has no plans on breaking from the core beliefs that helped set the foundation of the program. The approach has helped the Roadrunners consistently rebound from setbacks under Traylor, and as UTSA prepares to host North Texas at 8 p.m. Saturday in the Alamodome with conference title hopes still in the balance, receiver Mekhi Anderson said the team's confidence has never wavered. "It's just fighting for your brothers, knowing just that you have guys that's with you through everything," Anderson said. "Through any challenging moments or any adversity, we just keep fighting. Offensive lineman Luke Lapeze, who stands as the longest tenured Roadrunner after joining the team in 2021, said that idea was central to UTSA's culture long before they gave it a name. Cummins has hit out at Khawaja for claiming the bowlers knew about Sandpaper use in Cape Town. Cummins stood by the bowlers' statement from 2021. Cummins finally responds to Khawaja's allegations about Sandpapergate Australia's Test and ODI captain Pat Cummins has finally addressed the controversy that has rocked Australian cricket in the last one week. It all started after former national team opener Usman Khawaja made explosive claims about the infamous 'Sandpapergate' from 2018 during Australia's tour of South Africa. In his recently released autobiography, 'Sabr', Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian team from the 2018 South Africa tour was aware of the use of sandpaper in Cape Town and not just the three players who were implicated. The official line from Cricket Australia since the incident in Cape Town has held that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the third Test against South Africa. The aim, as understood at the time, was to scuff the surface and help the ball swing in reverse, and the three men were handed bans of up upto 12 months for their roles. However, Khawaja's claims in his book have brought the incident back into the limelight, as the southpaw said every Australian player knew about it, including the bowlers. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images It was a heated scene at the Toyota Center on Wednesday, where the Golden State Warriors and Houston Rockets faced off for the first time this season. With nearly identical records and stars on both sides, we expected a highly competitive matchup , but nobody was prepared for the violence that followed. With both teams battling hard, tensions boiled over late in the third quarter when veteran guard Marcus Smart got tangled up with Warriors big man Charles Bassey . Smart was ejected after connecting on a punch at mid-court, and the league announced further punishment today: a three-game suspension. “The NBA is suspending Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games for punching Golden State center Charles Bassey on Wednesday night,” reported ESPN’s Shams Charania . In physical altercations like this, the NBA often responds with fines or suspensions for those involved. Usually, however, the suspension is limited to one game, allowing for a quick return. In this case, the NBA came down harder, no doubt because Smart actually connected with a punch to the face. He had been tussling with Smart for a while by that point, and Rockets coach Ime Udoka says he had personally challenged Smart to take physical action. “I didn’t see it, but Marcus started talking to him, and he says they got wrapped up and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up,” said Udoka after the game . “So he said something to him, and Bassey said, ‘What you gonna do?’ and he did it.” Bassey did not receive any punishment from the altercation, but he sure had a lot to say after yesterday’s game. With a smile, he called Smart “fake tough” and “dirty” for getting physical over a purely basketball play. Now, Bassey will move on to the next game, while Marcus has to spend a week on the sidelines. Smart, 32, joined the Rockets this summer after a short stint with the Lakers . Wanting a place where he could play a big role on a contending team, he felt Houston was a good fit, if for nothing else than a chance to reunite with his former coach, Ime Udoka. So far, the results have been impressive. This season, at 9-3, the Rockets are third in the West, just 1.5 games back from the No. 1-seeded Lakers. item.description: Tennessee guard Juke Harris (2) attempts a shot past Radford guard Mathieu Grujicic (9) during a college basketball game between Tennessee and Radford at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center in Knoxville on Nov. 9, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s early, but the Juke Harris-Tennessee marriage is off to a slow start — that may be putting it mildly. Through two official games, Harris has just 13 total points. The Wake Forest transfer scored seven points in the home opener against Wofford, then just six points against Radford on Monday. Harris is 3-13 from the field and 2-9 from three-point range. This production is a continuation of what we saw during the preseason scrimmages against Xavier and Duke. “I think for Juke this is a new experience,” Tennessee assistant coach Earl Grant said on Thursday. “He played 32 minutes a game last year, averaged 20 points a game. He took the most attempts on his team, played the most minutes. And his team depended on him to be their leading scorer all the time. I think now he’s on a team with a lot of guys who can do a lot of things.” Harris played 35 minutes per game last season for the Demon Deacons, averaging over 21 points per game. He shot 44 percent from the field while handing a near 30 percent usage rate. So far this season, Harris has a 17.7 percent usage rate. That’s a number that’s likely to tick up quickly, but as Grant noted, Tennessee isn’t short on options. Terrence Hill Jr. has proven to be the creator to this point. We’ve also seen Tyler Lundblade and Dai Dai Ames handle the ball and create quite a bit through two games. Troy Henderson has also gotten in on the action. Still, the upside of this team likely travels through Harris, who has proven plenty capable of carrying a roster before. “He’s trying to carve out what he has to do for Tennessee basketball for Tennessee basketball to win,” Grant continued. “And I think scoring is a big part of that, but he’s gotta defend, he’s gotta rebound, he’s gotta lead, he’s gotta talk. And he’s had more people around him that can score, as well, so he may have to facilitate at times.” For Rick Barnes, it’s a moving target. He’s likely going to tinker with his starting lineups and rotations over the next several weeks. However, after Friday’s game against Tennessee State, things begin getting very real. The Volunteers welcome Michigan State — fresh off of a win over Duke this week — to Food City Center on Tuesday. The Players Era Tournament gets going a week after that in Las Vegas. Getting Harris going would certainly be a massive boost heading into that massive event on Thanksgiving week.

item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: Credit: NBC Sports; Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Notre Dame’s Thursday media availability typically traffics in injury updates and opponent scouting, but Marcus Freeman devoted his opening remarks to the broadcaster who was supposed to be in the NBC booth on Saturday. Dan Hicks’ death at 64 following an acute illness was announced Thursday morning, a sudden and staggering loss for an NBC Sports operation that had leaned on his steady hand for more than three decades and had penciled him in to call the Fighting Irish against the Eagles on Saturday. But more importantly, he was a great husband, father and man.” — Jack Soble (@jacksoble56) November 12, 2026 Freeman’s decision to celebrate Hicks as a husband and father before a broadcaster mirrored the remembrance Storm shared earlier that morning. item.title: Dodgers Miss Out on Major MLB Awards Despite 100-Win Season
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers had several candidates for end-of-season awards in 2026 following their 100-win season, but none of their representatives brought home awards. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dave Roberts and Tanner Scott all received votes for major awards on Wednesday, but none of them managed to place first in voting. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Yoshinobu Yamamoto Yamamoto, unsurprisingly, was one of the front runners for the Cy Young, but he fell short despite his strong season. The Milwaukee Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski unanimously won the award , with Yamamoto coming in fourth behind the Philadelphia Phillies’ Cristopher Sanchez and the Atlanta Braves’ Chris Sale. The Dodgers’ right-hander received just two second-place votes, as well as seven third-place votes, 14 fourth-place votes and six fifth-place votes for 63 points—35 points behind Sale. Yamamoto had an exceptional year, posting a 2.53 ERA through 28 starts while striking out 182 batters in 185 innings pitched, earning his second All-Star appearance. 2026 marks the second consecutive year Yamamoto earned Cy Young votes, as he finished third behind Sanchez and Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes last year. He placed fifth among National League managers this season , with Brewers manager Pat Murphy taking home the award with 20 first-place votes. Also ahead of Roberts are the Braves’ Walt Weiss, Phillies’ Don Mattingly and the San Diego Padres’ Craig Stammen. Roberts led the Dodgers to their first 100-win season since 2023 this past season. Tanner Scott Scott also lost out to a unanimous winner in NL Reliever of the Year voting , as Padres closer Mason Miller took the award home. He also finished behind the Phillies’ Jhoan Duran, Brewers’ Trevor Megill, Padres’ Adrian Morejón, Braves’ Raisel Iglesias, Pirates’ Mason Montgomery and Braves’ Didier Fuentes. Scott had a solid bounceback year following a tumultuous first year in Los Angeles , posting a 2.69 ERA with the Dodgers over the course of 69 appearances with the team. He logged a career-high 25 saves over the course of the season, striking out 82 batters through 63.2 innings pitched. While the Dodgers lost out on these three awards, they still have the opportunity to take home awards like the Silver Slugger, which MLB will announce Nov. 17, and the MVP, which MLB will announce Thursday at 4:00 p.m. PT. item.title: Throwback Thursday: The time Tony Gonzalez was almost traded
item.description: With the NFL Trade Deadline passing this week, it’s a good time to remember an era when the Kansas City Chiefs were more often sellers than buyers at this time of year. We ask @JayGlazer about the craziest trade that never happened. 👀 pic.twitter.com/Z14VL98lUR — Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) November 11, 2026 Wednesday morning, on “The Dan Patrick Show,” Fox Sports NFL Insider shared a story about former Chiefs tight end Tony Gonzalez nearly being traded midseason. He reminisced about negotiations between Kansas City and two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles , led by head coach Andy Reid, and the Green Bay Packers , led by Mike McCarthy. “Tony Gonzalez wants to get traded from the Chiefs, right?” Glazer remembered. “At the time, Carl Peterson was the GM; he had two deals: one with the Eagles and one with the Packers. Andy Reid and the Eagles were offered a [third-round pick] and LJ Smith, their tight end, and the Packers were offered a three and whoever their tight end was.” Glazer is most likely referring to the 2008 season, a lost year in Kansas City that featured a 2-14 record. The year before, the Chiefs went 4-12. The Packers tight end he was likely referring to was Donald Lee, but Green Bay also had 21-year-old Jermichael Finley on the 2008 team. “This is Tony: he talked to the Chiefs. He wanted to finish his career on a contender,” Glazer recalled. “He wanted to go somewhere else, and they agreed. So they’re really going back and forth, and it’s really up to him.” “Maybe 20 minutes before, Carl Peterson changes it from a three to a two, and there just wasn’t enough time to do it, right? I got a text from Andy Reid like, ‘I knew this wasn’t going to happen.’ I got a text from McCarthy: furious.” Glazer told Patrick that Gonzalez lost it when hearing that the trade didn’t go through. He was ready to put the Chiefs on blast for not letting him leave town: “Get your pen out!” “He wanted to do a story that there was no way we could ever publish in the history of life,” Glazer said. “I never do stories where someone is just emotional… he was like ‘I’m never playing!‘” “He calmed down — might’ve taken a couple of days off — and went out and finished with Kansas City,” Glazer finished. “Eventually, him and Scott Pioli and Todd Haley were horrible, and they traded him to Atlanta.” Gonzalez was traded to the Atlanta Falcons the following spring in 2009, and finally won a playoff game in the Divisional Round of the 2012 season. If the trade had gone through with Green Bay, Tony G could’ve had his Super Bowl ring with the 2010 Packers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Too bad.
